label: Second copy step (recall_idx 1) of long sequences, boosted when early tokens are b/3/h/g/u/j
explanation: Fires only at step L+1, the first step after <DEL> (input = original token 0, output = original token 1). It never fires in the original phase, at the delimiter, or at later copy steps. recall_idx==1 alone covers ~100% of activations but only 9.6% of those steps are active. The firing rate rises steeply with L: L=9 gives 64% of the mass and L=8 gives 27%, while L<=6 is nearly silent. Within those steps, firing and magnitude depend on content: it is strongly enriched when original token 1 or 2 (the current or next output) is b, 3, h, g, u or j, with b strongest. The top examples nearly all have b or bb at positions 1-2. Restricting to L>=8 with that token condition gives dev F1 0.58 and mass 0.77. The simpler (recall_idx==1)&(L>=8) gives F1 0.40 and mass 0.91. The residual looks like a graded, additive token-content score that a boolean predicate cannot capture.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the next token to output (most: b, 3, g, h, u, j; least: o, c, n, x) and the token being output (most: b, 3, g, h, u, j; least: 1, o, c, n); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=9 & t=10, L=8 & t=9.
